Explanation of the words:

Fatir as-samawati wal-ard (Originator of the heavens and the earth): i.e., their Creator without any precedent model.

Ja'il al-mala'ikati rusulan (Who made the angels messengers): i.e., He made from them messengers to the prophets, such as Jibril (peace be upon him).

Uli ajnihah (Possessing wings): i.e., possessors of wings, plural of janah (wing), like the wing of a bird.

Yazidu fil-khalqi ma yasha' (He adds to creation whatever He wills): i.e., He adds to the three whatever He wills, for Jibril has six hundred wings.

Wa ma yumsik (And whatever He withholds): i.e., of mercy, from Allah, so no one can release it besides Him, glorified and exalted is He.

Wa huwa al-'Aziz al-Hakim (And He is the Mighty, the Wise): i.e., the Dominant over His affair, the Wise in His management and His workmanship.

Udhkuru ni'mata Allahi 'alaykum (Remember the favor of Allah upon you): i.e., remember His favors, exalted is He, upon you in creating you, providing for you, and granting you security in your sanctuary.

Hal min khaliqin ghayru Allahi yarzuqukum (Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you): i.e., there is no creator for you other than Allah, and no provider who provides for you.

Min as-sama'i wal-ard? (From the heaven and the earth?): i.e., by sending down rain from the sky and causing crops to grow from the earth.

La ilaha illa Huwa (There is no deity except Him): i.e., there is no worshipped one in truth except Him; therefore worship Him and declare His oneness.

Fa-anna tu'fakun (How then are you turned away?): i.e., how are you diverted from His oneness, while you acknowledge that He alone is the Creator and Provider.

The meaning of the verses:

The words of the Most High, ﴿All praise is for Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾: i.e., complete thanks and perfect praise belong to Allah by right. The statement is in the form of a report, but its meaning is an command, i.e., say, "All praise is for Allah." And thank Him as He is. It is also a report from Him, exalted is He, that praise belongs to Him and that none other deserves it, and that this is what necessitates His praise. ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾: i.e., He created them without any precedent model or pattern imitated in their creation. ﴿Who made the angels messengers﴾: i.e., messengers to the prophets and to whomever of His servants He wills, by inspiration and true dreams. The words ﴿possessing wings﴾ describe the angels: i.e., possessors of wings, ﴿two, two, and three, three, and four, four﴾. The words ﴿He adds to creation﴾: i.e., He adds to the creation of wings whatever He wills; He created for Jibril (peace be upon him) six hundred wings, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reported in the authentic collections, and He adds to the creation of whatever He wills of His creatures, and He is over all things Competent.

The words of the Most High, ﴿Whatever Allah grants to people of mercy, none can withhold it, and whatever He withholds, none can release it after Him﴾: He, exalted is He, informs that the keys of everything are in His hand. Whatever He opens for people of provision, goodness and blessing, none of His creatures can withhold it apart from Him; and whatever He withholds of that, none of His creatures can release it. He alone is the Mighty, Dominant over His command and will; there is no preventer of what He gives and no repeller of what He decrees, the Wise in His workmanship and the management of His creation. The words of the Most High: ﴿O mankind, remember the favor of Allah upon you﴾: this is His address to the people of Makkah from the Quraysh, commanding them to remember His favors upon them in that He created them, widened their provision, and made for them a secure sanctuary while people are snatched away from around them in fear. He commands them to remember His favor, because when they remember it they will thank Him by believing in Him and declaring His oneness.

He is the One who created them and provided for them from the heaven and the earth. The heaven sends rain and the earth brings forth growth by His command. Therefore, ﴿there is no deity except Him﴾, i.e., there is no worshipped one in truth except Him. So how then are you turned away from the truth after knowing it? Indeed your condition is astonishing.

This is what is indicated by the words of the Most High: ﴿Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? There is no deity except Him, so how are you turned away?﴾

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 35, verses 4–7:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And if they deny you﴾: that is, O Our Messenger, regarding what you have brought of monotheism (tawhid), and the creed of resurrection and recompense, and they do not believe in you.

﴿Certainly, messengers before you were denied﴾: that is, you are not alone in being denied; so do not despair and do not grieve, and be patient as those before you were patient.

﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾: and He will surely requite the deniers for their denial and the patient for their patience.

﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you about Allah﴾: that is, let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah, namely concerning His forbearance and His granting of respite; the Deceiver is Satan.

﴿So take him as an enemy﴾: that is, do not obey him, and do not accept what he deceives you with, and obey your Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿He only invites his party﴾: that is, his followers in falsehood, disbelief, evil and corruption.

﴿That they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾: that is, so that their affair ends with them being among the people of the blazing Fire.

﴿For them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾: that is, for them is forgiveness of their sins and a great reward in Paradise, because of their faith and their righteous deeds.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah, the Exalted, established the proof against the polytheists in the preceding verses, He said to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿And if they deny you﴾ after you have established the proof against them, you are not alone as a denier; many messengers before you were denied, who came to their peoples with clear proofs and scriptures and were patient. So be patient as they were patient. ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾: judgment will be passed between you and them in truth; He will grant you victory in this world and disgrace them, and He will show you mercy in the Hereafter and punish them.

And His saying: ﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is true﴾: that is, O people of Makkah and every deceived person among mankind who is deluded by the life of this world, know that Allah's promise of resurrection and recompense is true. So let not the life of this world deceive you with the length of your lives, the health of your bodies, and the abundance of your provision, for that is surely going to pass away from you. ﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you about Allah﴾: that is, concerning His forbearance and His granting of respite. ﴿The Deceiver﴾ is Satan, who takes Allah's forbearance toward you and His granting you respite as a way to lead you astray and corrupt you, by urging you to delay repentance, persist in sins, and continue in them. ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you﴾, of extreme enmity, evident in its nature. So take him as an enemy yourselves, do not obey him, and do not respond to his call. ﴿He only invites his party﴾: that is, his followers ﴿to be among the companions of the Blaze﴾: that is, the blazing Fire. He wants you to be with him in Hellfire, for he is already judged to it from eternity. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment﴾: that is, in the Hereafter. And those who believe and do righteous deeds: ﴿for them is forgiveness﴾: that is, for their sins, ﴿and a great reward﴾: which is Paradise and the everlasting bliss within it. This is Allah's judgment concerning His servants and His decree regarding them: they are of two groups, a righteous believer and a corrupt disbeliever, and each has a just recompense.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Consolation of the Messenger ﷺ, and it includes all callers to truth: when they are denied and harmed, they must be patient.

2- Affirmation of resurrection and the recompense it entails, which is Allah's true promise.

3- Warning against being deceived by the world, that is, by long life, abundant provision, and bodily health.

4- Warning against Satan, and the obligation to acknowledge his enmity and treat him as an enemy: his speech is not to be accepted, his call is not to be answered, and one is not to be deceived by his adorning of ugliness and evil.

5- Explanation of the reward of the friends of the Most Merciful, who are the enemies of Satan, and the reward of the enemies of the Most Merciful, who are the friends of Satan.

﴿And if they deny you﴾: that is, O Our Messenger, regarding what you have brought of monotheism (tawhid), and the creed of resurrection and recompense, and they do not believe in you.

﴿Certainly, messengers before you were denied﴾: that is, you are not alone in being denied; so do not despair and do not grieve, and be patient as those before you were patient.

﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾: and He will surely requite the deniers for their denial and the patient for their patience.

﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you about Allah﴾: that is, let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah, namely concerning His forbearance and His granting of respite; the Deceiver is Satan.

﴿So take him as an enemy﴾: that is, do not obey him, and do not accept what he deceives you with, and obey your Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿He only invites his party﴾: that is, his followers in falsehood, disbelief, evil and corruption.

﴿That they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾: that is, so that their affair ends with them being among the people of the blazing Fire.

﴿For them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾: that is, for them is forgiveness of their sins and a great reward in Paradise, because of their faith and their righteous deeds.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah, the Exalted, established the proof against the polytheists in the preceding verses, He said to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿And if they deny you﴾ after you have established the proof against them, you are not alone as a denier; many messengers before you were denied, who came to their peoples with clear proofs and scriptures and were patient. So be patient as they were patient. ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾: judgment will be passed between you and them in truth; He will grant you victory in this world and disgrace them, and He will show you mercy in the Hereafter and punish them.

And His saying: ﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is true﴾: that is, O people of Makkah and every deceived person among mankind who is deluded by the life of this world, know that Allah's promise of resurrection and recompense is true. So let not the life of this world deceive you with the length of your lives, the health of your bodies, and the abundance of your provision, for that is surely going to pass away from you. ﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you about Allah﴾: that is, concerning His forbearance and His granting of respite. ﴿The Deceiver﴾ is Satan, who takes Allah's forbearance toward you and His granting you respite as a way to lead you astray and corrupt you, by urging you to delay repentance, persist in sins, and continue in them. ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you﴾, of extreme enmity, evident in its nature. So take him as an enemy yourselves, do not obey him, and do not respond to his call. ﴿He only invites his party﴾: that is, his followers ﴿to be among the companions of the Blaze﴾: that is, the blazing Fire. He wants you to be with him in Hellfire, for he is already judged to it from eternity. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment﴾: that is, in the Hereafter. And those who believe and do righteous deeds: ﴿for them is forgiveness﴾: that is, for their sins, ﴿and a great reward﴾: which is Paradise and the everlasting bliss within it. This is Allah's judgment concerning His servants and His decree regarding them: they are of two groups, a righteous believer and a corrupt disbeliever, and each has a just recompense.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Consolation of the Messenger ﷺ, and it includes all callers to truth: when they are denied and harmed, they must be patient.

2- Affirmation of resurrection and the recompense it entails, which is Allah's true promise.

3- Warning against being deceived by the world, that is, by long life, abundant provision, and bodily health.

4- Warning against Satan, and the obligation to acknowledge his enmity and treat him as an enemy: his speech is not to be accepted, his call is not to be answered, and one is not to be deceived by his adorning of ugliness and evil.

5- Explanation of the reward of the friends of the Most Merciful, who are the enemies of Satan, and the reward of the enemies of the Most Merciful, who are the friends of Satan.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 35, verses 8–11:

Explanation of the words:

"Afaman zuyyina lahu su'u 'amalihi": that is, the ugliness of his deeds, such as shirk and sins.

"Fa-ra'ahu hasanan": that is, he saw it as good and adorned, with no ugliness in it.

"Fa-la tadhhab nafsuka 'alayhim": that is, over those whom Satan has made the ugliness of their deeds seem fair to.

"Hasarat": that is, do not destroy yourself by grieving over them because of their disbelief.

"Inna Allaha 'alimun bima yasna'un": and He will recompense them for their false deeds.

"Fa-tutheeru sahaban": that is, He stirs it and drives it strongly so that it gathers and moves.

"Fa-saqnahu ila baladin mayyit": that is, a place with no vegetation.

"Fa-ahyayna bihi al-ard": that is, with plants, herbage, pasture and crops.

"Kadhalika al-nushur": that is, the resurrection and the second life.

"Fa-lillahi al-'izzatu jami'an": that is, let him seek honour by obeying Allah, for it is not attained except by that.

"Ilayhi yas'idu al-kalimu al-tayyib": that is, to Allah ascend the good words, which are "Subhan Allah," "al-hamdu lillah," and "Allahu akbar."

"Wa al-'amalu al-salihu yarfa'uhu": that is, performing the obligatory duties and voluntary acts raises the good words to Allah.

"Yamkuruna al-sayyi'at": that is, they do them and earn them.

"Wa makru ula'ika huwa yabur": that is, their deed is what perishes and comes to nothing.

"Khalaqakum min turab": that is, our origin, who is Adam.

"Thumma min nutfah": that is, from the water of the man and the water of the woman, and this is all of the offspring of Adam.

"Thumma ja'alakum azwajan": that is, male and female.

"Wa ma tahmilu min untha": that is, what a female carries of an embryo, and she does not bear it except with His permission.

"Wa ma yu'ammaru min mu'ammarin": that is, whatever is lengthened of the life of one whose life is long is only in a Book.

"Wa la yunqasu min 'umrihi": that is, by making it less and shorter than the long life, only in a Book.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in strengthening the spirit of the Messenger ﷺ and firming his resolve before the fluctuations, obstinacy and deceit of the polytheists. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Is one to whom the evil of his deed is made attractive so that he sees it as good...?﴾ That is, is one whom Satan and his own soul and desire have made the ugliness of his deed, which is shirk and sins, appear fair, so that he sees it as good, like one whom Allah has guided, who is upon light from his Lord, seeing good as good and evil as evil? The answer is: No, no. As for His saying: ﴿For indeed, Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾, He sends astray by His justice and according to His laws regarding misguidance whom He wills among His servants, and guides by His bounty whom He wills to guide. Therefore, O Messenger, do not let your soul go to waste in grief over their non-guidance, destroying yourself in sorrow over it. As for His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾, there is no need for sorrow and distress, since their Lord, who is He, has enumerated their deeds and will recompense them for them. As for the saying of the Exalted ﴿And Allah is He who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds﴾, that is, they agitate and move them. ﴿And We drive it to a dead land﴾, that is, with no plants or crops in it. ﴿And We revive thereby the earth after its death; thus is the resurrection﴾. That is, just as Allah the Exalted sends down water from the sky and revives the earth after its death, so He revives the dead, for after the passing of the world, Allah the Exalted will send down water from beneath the Throne, and man will grow from a bone called "ajb al-dhanab," and his creation will be completed. Then Allah the Exalted will send the souls, and each soul will enter its body, and no soul will mistake its body.

Thus, just as the process of reviving the earth through plants is completed, so the process of reviving the dead is completed, and they will be driven to the gathering place, and every soul will be recompensed for what it earned, and Allah is swift in reckoning.

As for the saying of the Exalted ﴿Whoever desires honour, then to Allah belongs all honour﴾, let him seek it from Allah by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger, for honour belongs entirely to Allah; the honourable is one whom Allah honours, and the humiliated is one whom He humiliates. They used to seek honour through idols, so know that whoever desires honour should seek it from its Owner. As for one who does not possess honour, how could he give it to another? Indeed, one who lacks a thing cannot give it. As for His saying ﴿To Him ascend the good words﴾, that is, to Allah ascend the good words, and the righteous deed raises them to Allah the Exalted. So if there is a statement without action, it is not raised to Allah and is not rewarded. Allah the Exalted has condemned those who say and do not act, saying: ﴿Greatly hateful is it in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do﴾ [al-Saff: 3]. As for His saying ﴿And those who plot evil deeds﴾, that is, they do them, and they are shirk and sins: ﴿for them is a severe punishment﴾, this is their recompense. ﴿And the plotting of those is what will perish﴾, that is, the plotting of those who do evil deeds ﴿will perish﴾, that is, it will be corrupted and nullified.

As for the saying of the Exalted ﴿And Allah created you from dust﴾, that is, He created our origin from dust, who is Adam; then He created us, his descendants, from a drop, which is the water of the man and the water of the woman. ﴿Then He made you pairs﴾, that is, male and female. These are manifestations of divine power, requiring His worship and monotheism, and necessitating resurrection and recompense. As for His saying ﴿And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge, and no one is granted long life or has his life shortened except that it is in a Book﴾, that is, it is increased in his life, and not decreased from his life, except that it is in a Book, which is the Book of Decrees. This is a manifestation of His knowledge, and with knowledge and power He is capable of reviving the dead and resurrecting people for reckoning and recompense. Therefore the Exalted said ﴿Indeed, that﴾, that is, what has been mentioned of creation and governance and its existence in the Book of Decrees, ﴿is easy for Allah﴾, that is, simple, with no difficulty in it.

Guidance from the verses:

1- A warning against following desire and yielding to Satan, for that leads the servant to come to see evil deeds as good, and then he is deprived of Allah's guidance and is never guided; this results from persistence in sins and transgressions.

2- The reviving of the earth after its death is clear evidence for the resurrection of people alive after their death.

3- The pursuit of honour is a precious aim, and it is obedience to Allah and His Messenger; no one attains true honour without obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

4- The knowledge of Allah manifest in creation and governance, to which is added His power that nothing can frustrate; by both, creation, resurrection and recompense are accomplished.

5- Affirmation of resurrection and recompense, and affirmation of the Book of Decrees, which is the Preserved Tablet.

4- The knowledge of Allah manifest in creation and governance, to which is added His power that nothing can frustrate; by both, creation, resurrection and recompense are accomplished.

He is the Truth about which there is no doubt.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 35, verses 15–18:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Antumu al-fuqara'u ila Allah﴾ (You are the needy towards Allah): i.e., those who are in need of Him in every state.

﴿Wa Allahu huwa al-Ghaniyyu al-Hamid﴾ (And Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy): i.e., He is free of need of you, O people, and of all His creation, praised for His acts, His words and His good management. All creatures praise Him because of their need for Him and His independence from them.

﴿Wa ya'ti bi-khalqin jadid﴾ (And bring a new creation): i.e., in your place.

﴿Wa ma dhalika 'ala Allahi bi-'aziz﴾ (And that is not difficult for Allah): i.e., it is not something impossible or unattainable; rather it is easy and feasible to occur.

﴿Wa la taziru waziratun wizra ukhra﴾ (No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another): i.e., in the judgement of Allah and His decree among His servants, a sinful soul that carries its own sin does not bear the sin of another soul; rather every bearer bears its own burden alone.

﴿Wa in tad'u muthqalatun﴾ (And if one heavy-laden calls out): i.e., heavy with its burdens, so that it cannot walk or move.

﴿La yuhmalu minhu shay'un﴾ (None of it will be carried): i.e., it will not find anyone who responds to it and bears any part of its sin, even if it calls upon its son, its father or its mother, let alone others. This is the ruling of Allah, the Exalted.

﴿Yakhshawna rabbahum bil-ghayb﴾ (They fear their Lord unseen): i.e., because they have not seen Him with their eyes.

﴿Wa man tazakka﴾ (And whoever purifies himself): i.e., cleanses his soul from polytheism and sins.

مختلف ألوانه كذلك (mukhtalif alwanuh kadhalik): i.e., like the variation of fruits, mountains and paths within them.

To Him belongs all praise and favour.

1- Demonstration of the manifestations of divine power and knowledge in the variation of colours, natures and essences.

2- Knowledge is the path to fear: whoever has no knowledge of Allah has no fear of Him; it is only those of His servants who have knowledge who truly fear Allah.

3- The merit of reciting the noble Qur'an, establishing prayer, and giving zakat and charity.

4- Describing Allah as Forgiving and Appreciative is an encouragement for sinners to repent, and for doers of good to increase.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 35, verses 31–35:

Explanation of the words:

"From the Book": i.e., the noble Qur'an.

"Confirming what is before it": i.e., of the previous scriptures, such as the Torah (al-Tawrah) and the Gospel (al-Injil).

"Then We caused the Book to be inherited": i.e., the books that preceded the Qur'an, since their essence is contained in the noble Qur'an.

"Those whom We have chosen": i.e., We chose the believers from the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ).

"Among them is one who wrongs himself": by committing sins.

"And among them is one who is moderate": one who performs the obligatory duties (fara'id) and avoids the major sins (kaba'ir).

"And among them is one who is foremost in good deeds": one who performs the obligatory duties and the voluntary acts of worship (nawafil) and avoids the major and minor sins (saghair).

"By Allah's permission": i.e., by His grant of success and His guidance.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 35, verses 36–39:

Explanation of the words:

Lā yuqḍā ʿalayhim (They shall not be given a decree to die): i.e., by death, so that they would die and find rest.

Kadhālika najzī kulla kafūr (Thus We recompense every ungrateful disbeliever): i.e., thus is the recompense; We recompense every disbeliever who is ungrateful toward Us, toward Our signs, and toward Our meeting.

Wa-hum yaṣṭarikhūna fīhā (They will cry out therein): i.e., they will shout at the top of their voices, seeking to be taken out of it.

Yaqūlūn (They will say): i.e., in their wailing and screaming, "Our Lord, take us out" of it, "that we may do righteousness."

Awa lam nuʿammirkum mā yatadhakkaru fīh (Did We not give you a life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed?): i.e., a span of time in which whoever wished to be mindful would be mindful.

Wa-jāʾakum al-nadhīr (And the warner came to you): i.e., the Messenger, but you did not respond and persisted in polytheism and sins.

Innahu ʿalīmun bidhāt al-ṣudūr (Indeed He is Knowing of what is in the breasts): i.e., of what is in the hearts, including persistence in disbelief, even if the disbeliever lived his whole life.

Khalāʾif fī al-arḍ (Successors on the earth): one of you succeeds another. Khalāʾif is the plural of khalīfah, meaning one who succeeds another.

Fa-ʿalayhi kufruh (Upon him is his disbelief): i.e., the burden of his disbelief.

Illā maqtan (Except increased abhorrence): i.e., except intense anger upon them from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Illā khasāran (Except loss): i.e., in the Hereafter, when they will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.

Meaning of the verses:

After Allah, Exalted is He, mentioned the recompense of the people of faith and righteous deeds, He mentioned the recompense of the people of disbelief and sins, saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved﴾, i.e., in Allah, His signs, and His meeting, ﴿for them is the fire of Hell﴾, i.e., as their recompense. ﴿It will not be decreed for them﴾, i.e., by death, so that they would die and find rest, and their punishment would not be lightened for them even for a moment. His statement, Exalted is He, ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., such is the recompense, ﴿We recompense every ungrateful disbeliever﴾, i.e., one who exceeds in disbelief and persists in it. His statement: ﴿And they will cry out therein﴾, i.e., in Hell, meaning they will shout at the top of their voices in weeping and wailing, saying: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out﴾, i.e., from the Fire, and return us to the worldly life ﴿that we may do righteousness, other than what we used to do﴾, i.e., of polytheism and sins. It will be said to them: ﴿Did We not give you a life long enough﴾, i.e., do you seek to leave the Fire so that you may do righteousness, when We did not prolong your lives such that whoever wished to take heed could take heed therein? ﴿And the warner came to you﴾, i.e., but you did not respond to him and persisted in polytheism and sins. So taste (the punishment), for ﴿the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., those who wronged themselves through polytheism and sins, have no helper who will rescue them from the Fire. His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., all that is hidden in the heavens and the earth, ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾, and among that is that He knows what is in your hearts and what you persisted in of polytheism, evil, and corruption, even if you lived your whole lifetime.

His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿It is He who has made you successors upon the earth﴾, i.e., one of you succeeds another. In this is that which enables admonition and reflection, for the wise is one who takes a lesson from others. Nations before you perished for their sins, so why do you not take warning from them, since you have succeeded them and come after them? Therefore there is no excuse for you at all.

After this clarification, whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief; he himself bears its consequence. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 35, verses 44–45:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And they were mightier than them in strength﴾: That is, Allah destroyed them because of their denial of their messengers.

﴿Nor is there anything in the heavens or on earth that could ever escape Him﴾: That is, that it could outrun Him and elude Him, so that He would be unable to reach it.

﴿Indeed He is ever Knowing, Competent﴾: That is, Knowing of all things and Competent over all of them.

﴿For what they earned﴾: That is, for their sins and disobediences.

﴿He would not leave upon it [the earth] any creature﴾: That is, upon the surface of the earth, any living being (dābba), meaning every soul that moves upon the earth, which is every living thing.

﴿Until an appointed term﴾: That is, the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Indeed Allah is ever Seeing of His servants﴾: So He will call them to account and recompense them according to their earnings, whether good or evil.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah threatened the polytheists by carrying out His custom (sunnah) concerning them, which is the punishment and destruction of the deniers if they persist in denial and do not repent, He said: ﴿Have they not travelled in the land﴾, that is, the polytheists who deny Our Messenger, ﴿to the north or to the south﴾, ﴿so that they might see what was the end of those before them﴾, such as the people of Ṣāliḥ and the people of Hūd. Indeed, their end was destruction and loss. ﴿And they were mightier than them in strength﴾: that is, than these polytheists of today in strength. As for His saying, ﴿Nor is there anything in the heavens or on earth that could ever escape Him﴾: that is, nothing can overpower Allah so that it escapes Him and flees from Him, nor can it be beyond His power; rather He is overpowering over everything and dominant over it. His saying, ﴿Indeed He is ever Knowing, Competent﴾, affirms His power and the powerlessness of everything before Him, for the All-Knowing, All-Competent cannot be overcome by hiding and concealment, nor by resistance and flight.

As for His saying, ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for what they have earned, He would not leave upon it [the earth] any creature﴾, which is the last verse of this passage [45]: that is, if Allah were to take people to account for their sins, then everyone who sinned would be requited and destroyed, and He would leave upon the surface of the earth no living soul that moves upon it. But He, exalted is He, delays the wrongdoers ﴿until an appointed term﴾, that is, a specified time that is determined: if it is in this world, then it is in this world; and if it is the Day of Resurrection, then it is on the Day of Resurrection. His saying, ﴿So when their term comes, indeed Allah is ever Seeing of His servants﴾, informs that when the term of the wrongdoers comes, He, exalted is He, sees them, and not one of them is hidden from Him, so He destroys them and leaves none of them, because of His perfect knowledge and great power. Unquestionably, let the wrongdoers fear Allah.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The legitimacy of travelling in the land for the sake of reflection, not for leisure, amusement and play.

2. The clarification that nothing can overpower Allah, because of His knowledge and power, a state that necessitates fear of Him, may He be exalted, and turning back to Him.

3. The prohibition of seeking to hasten the punishment, for every matter has a term and a specified time before which it does not occur, so there is no sense at all in hastening it.
